instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Prove Your Loyalty
cards.instruction: Invent small tests of loyalty and judge every response without admitting there is a test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Choose the reunion photo. Mine includes the whole group; Sam's cuts two people off.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sam's is sharper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Focus is one criterion, not the entire selection process. Would you at least put mine first in the committee email?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send them side by side, the same size.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Order still guides attention. Put mine on the left, please; I spent Sunday fixing your slideshow.

beats.text: Keep Friday free in case I need moving help. A sensible plan includes contingency time.

beats.speaker: A

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Give It Up
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me catalogue your medal for the charity auction. We need its actual event and year, not just 'old medal.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only thing I've ever won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then provenance matters. I'll catalogue your name and result, not just the metal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I lend it for display instead? I still want people to know I won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A loan isn't an auction lot. Present it to the buyer yourself; I'll introduce you as the winner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sell the signed guitar and we can replace the fridge. Please don't polish the signature; that's the part a buyer will pay for.

beats.speaker: B

cards.title: Helpful Culprit
cards.instruction: Hide that the problem is your fault while enthusiastically helping investigate it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't sweep yet. We establish how the vase broke before we disturb the pieces.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why have you got glue on your fingers?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We identify the adhesive before drawing conclusions. Bring me the tube, by the cap, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's a piece of the vase stuck to your thumb.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then photograph it before we remove it. Honestly, must I label my own thumb for you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll investigate the dead office plant. Please don't empty the pot; we need the liquid as it was.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You watered it with your coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll compare it with a fresh cup from the machine. A source is not a conclusion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You put six sugars in yours. The machine didn't do that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Six in the comparison cup, then. Label it, please. I would like one properly prepared sample before we assign blame.

cards.title: Not That Subject
cards.instruction: Choose one subject you cannot let the scene reach. Redirect whenever the conversation gets close.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've booked your car into the garage. Let me fill in the repair form; mechanics need precise terminology.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What happened to my car?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We start with the registration, not speculation. Can you read it to me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I know the registration. I want to know why the door won't close.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: 'Door' is insufficient. Driver's side or passenger's side? Please let me complete one field properly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the rent letter there and hold this curtain rail. A level line matters more than how it looks from the sofa.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The landlord wants an answer today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then he can have a photograph of a properly finished room. Your end is dropping; lift it two inches.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's level. I'll send the photo and ask how much we owe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not from that angle. You'll make the rail look crooked. Hand me the phone and stand directly beneath it. Directly, please.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Merciful Lie
cards.instruction: Choose a truth your character believes would hurt someone. Keep it from them, even as honesty becomes harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The bakery assessed your cake in the wrong category. This is display work; put the knife away.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They wrote 'inedible.' I thought I'd finally made something worth selling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Display pieces aren't sliced. I'll prepare a card naming the materials and giving the price.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take it in and ask them to taste it while they read your card.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No tasting. We have just established the category. Give me the knife; I'll speak to them myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't call this a rejected poem. The magazine has the wrong format for it; we need a booklet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: If you think it's bad too, I'll stop writing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You are confusing format with quality. I'll write the cover description: 'A voice that deserves more space.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Put 'recommended by' and your name above it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Below the description, in smaller type. Please send me the proof; I would like my name to be the one thing they cannot criticise.
